docs.title: F1 Dashboard
docs.text: Streamlit dashboard showing the 5 fastest laps per circuit using the OpenF1 API.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Real-time lap time data via OpenF1 API
  • Top 5 fastest laps per session with driver comparison
  • Interactive Plotly charts
  • Configurable via environment variables

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Install dependencies
poetry install --with dev

# Start the dashboard
poetry run streamlit run src/f1/dashboard.py

The dashboard will be available at http://localhost:8501.

docs.title: Lap
docs.text:
Represents a single lap recorded during a session.

Field Type Description driver_number int Car number lap_duration float \| None Lap time in seconds lap_number int Lap number within the session session_key int Unique session identifier

docs.title: Driver
docs.text:
Represents an F1 driver.

Field Type Description driver_number int Car number full_name str Driver full name team_name str Constructor name name_acronym str 3-letter code (e.g. VER)

docs.title: Session
docs.text:
Represents a race weekend session.

Field Type Description session_key int Unique identifier session_name str Name (e.g. Race, Qualifying) date_start datetime Session start time (UTC) location str Circuit location

docs.title: filter_valid_laps(laps)
docs.text: Returns only laps where lap_duration is a positive number.

docs.title: build_driver_index(drivers)
docs.text: Returns a dict[int, Driver] mapping driver_number to Driver.

docs.title: compute_top_n_laps(laps, n)
docs.text: Returns the n fastest laps sorted ascending by lap_duration.

docs.title: F1DashboardService
docs.text:
service = F1DashboardService(
    lap_repo=...,
    driver_repo=...,
    session_repo=...,
)

data = service.get_top_laps(session_key=9159, top_n=5)

Returns a list of dicts ready for display, each containing driver name, team, lap number, and duration.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: The project follows a layered architecture with clear separation of concerns.

docs.title: Layer Overview
docs.text:
src/f1/
├── utils/          # Cross-cutting concerns (logger, config)
├── domain/         # Business models, repository ABCs, service
├── processing/     # Pure data transformation functions
├── ingestion/      # HTTP client + OpenF1 API adapters
└── dashboard.py    # Streamlit composition root

docs.title: Utils
docs.text:
• utils/logger.py — get_logger(name) returns a configured Python logger
  • utils/config.py — reads environment variables (base URL, timeouts, etc.)

docs.title: Domain
docs.text:
• domain/models.py — Pydantic v2 models: Lap, Driver, Session
  • domain/repositories.py — abstract base classes (LapRepository, DriverRepository, SessionRepository)
  • domain/services.py — F1DashboardService orchestrates repos to produce dashboard data

docs.title: Processing
docs.text:
• processing/lap_processor.py — pure functions:
    • filter_valid_laps — removes laps with missing or invalid times
    • build_driver_index — maps driver number to Driver object
    • compute_top_n_laps — returns the N fastest laps for each driver

docs.title: Ingestion
docs.text:
• ingestion/http_client.py — HttpClient with configurable retry logic
  • ingestion/openf1_client.py — concrete repository implementations against the OpenF1 REST API

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text: • dashboard.py — Streamlit app that wires all layers together (composition root)

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
OpenF1 API
    └─► HttpClient (retry)
        └─► OpenF1Repositories
            └─► F1DashboardService
                └─► lap_processor (filter + rank)
                    └─► Streamlit UI (Plotly charts)

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.12+
  • Poetry 2.x

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
git clone <repo>
cd F1
poetry install --with dev

Copy the environment file and adjust as needed:

cp .env.example .env

docs.title: Running Tests
docs.text:
# Unit tests only (fast, no network)
poetry run task test

# All tests including integration (requires network)
poetry run task test-all

Coverage threshold is set at 50%. Current coverage: ~75%.

docs.title: Linting and Formatting
docs.text:
poetry run task lint        # check
poetry run task lint-fix    # auto-fix
poetry run task format      # format with ruff
poetry run task format-check

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
# Live preview with hot-reload
poetry run task docs

# Build static site to site/
poetry run task docs-build

Hooks run ruff check and ruff format --check on every commit.
